target_customer: Mobile gamers (initially Gen Z players of Brawl Stars) who want voice chat and teammates, plus indie game developers who build on the Rune SDK
problem: Mobile games had weak social and voice features, so players struggled to find friends and teammates and to talk while playing. Later the problem became that indie multiplayer games needed backend work and an audience.
business_model: Free consumer app with an SDK and games platform; no revenue model stated in sources
product_category: Social multiplayer gaming platform and voice chat

founders.name: Sanjay Guruprasad
education: Physics at IIT Madras (per YC page)
Left a PhD at MIT to start Rune (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC company page describes him as coding since childhood.

founders.name: Bjarke Felbo
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder with Guruprasad in the July 2024 Game Developer article; education and employers not found.

competitors.name: Discord mobile voice chat
competitors.what: Free voice and text chat that Discord extended to iOS and Android for talking while playing mobile games

technical_complexity.rationale: A background voice chat app with an AI matchmaking layer for one game (Brawl Stars) was within reach of a small team; the later SDK and multiplayer backend was harder.

defensibility.rationale: Friend graphs and a catalog of games could create network effects, but Discord and in-game chat could be used as substitutes and the first product depended on one publisher's game.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch in 2019 noted Brawl Stars had basic built-in matchmaking and limited chat. No source shows an incumbent copying Rune; the company changed direction on its own.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (Oct 2019) described players struggling to find compatible teammates and having limited in-game communication in Brawl Stars. The YC page cites over 50 million minutes of friends playing together on the platform.

branding.domain_note: Company site is rune.ai per the YC directory; no purchase story found.

identity.visual_style: A Dribbble portfolio lists a Dusk Design System dated August 2024 alongside Rune projects
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, aimed at friend groups and Gen Z

rebrands.why: Relaunch as a mobile multiplayer platform for Gen Z; reason not stated in the source
Game Developer article update says the company renamed itself back to Rune and the app would be called RuneMatch; reason not stated

branding.community_and_virality: Pocket Gamer and Game Developer covered the launches; no evidence of merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic one word name, shared with other products, and the company changed names twice in 2024, which suggests the identity did not stick.

pivots.from: AI matchmaking and voice chat for Brawl Stars players
pivots.to: Platform and SDK for indie multiplayer games with built-in voice chat
pivots.why: Not stated; the YC page describes the later platform and SDK

outcome_analysis: Rune raised a 2 million dollar seed in 2019 for AI teammate matching, then evolved into a social multiplayer games platform with an SDK and about 50 indie games. A reported 8 million dollar raise followed in July 2024 under the name Dusk, and the company went back to the name Rune two months later. It is still active but small, so the story is a long search for a durable product more than a clear breakout.
notes: The 2024 amount is described as a collective 8 million dollars, so it may be cumulative and include the 2019 seed; stage recorded as other. Dealroom and CB Insights list 2.15 million across two seeds (aggregators, not relied on). Game Developer says the founders earlier built a PUBG and Call of Duty companion app also called Rune. The Discord blog post is undated in the search result, so the competitor source_date is null.
